2609.23194.title: Enhancing speech representation learning with cross-modal knowledge transfer with HGNN under low resource settings: the case study of Yemba
2609.23194.paper_summary: Acoustic representation learning is crucial for speech processing, yet low-resource languages (LRLs) face severe data scarcity, limiting the effectiveness of traditional and self-supervised methods. As a promising alternative, in this work, we propose to enhance acoustic representation trough a cross-modal transfer knowledge approach, based on heterogeneous graph neural networks (HGNNs), where acoustic and linguistic entities are modeled as distinct node types within a unified graph. Through message-passing mechanisms, linguistic nodes explicitly transfer knowledge to acoustic nodes, enabling structured and interpretable cross-modal information flow. To highlight this knowledge transfer and its benefits, we measured standard clustering metrics as an intrinsic evaluation of acoustic representation, and to emphasize applicability, we performed isolated-word recognition tasks using an English benchmark and a Cameroonian language dataset in low resources settings . Results demonstrate that acoustic representations consistently benefit from linguistic knowledge propagated through the graph. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of explicit cross-modal knowledge transfer for acoustic representation learning using HGNNs, highlighting a promising direction for speech representation in low-resource settings.
2609.23194.paper_summary_zh: 聲學表示學習對語音處理至關重要，但低資源語言（LRLs）面臨嚴重的數據匱乏，限制了傳統和自我監督方法的有效性。作為一種有前景的替代方案，在本研究中，我們提出通過基於異質圖神經網絡（HGNNs）的跨模態轉移知識方法來增強聲學表示，其中聲學和語言實體被建模為統一圖中的不同節點類型。通過消息傳遞機制，語言節點明確地將知識轉移到聲學節點，從而實現結構化和可解釋的跨模態信息流。為了突出這種知識轉移及其好處，我們測量了標準聚類指標，作為聲學表示的內在評估，並為了強調應用性，我們在低資源環境中使用英語基準和喀麥隆語言數據集進行了孤立單詞識別任務。結果顯示，聲學表示持續受益於通過圖傳播的語言知識。據我們所知，這是首次使用HGNNs顯示明確的跨模態知識轉移以進行聲學表示學習，突顯了在低資源環境中語音表示的有前景方向。
